primaryCommitChecks.message:
Emit enough in program events to follow pool, quote and config state from logs (#791)

QuoteSet now carries the quote's stored payout addresses, so a reader can judge them without
reading the quote account. ReservationRequested carries its collateral_chain, which with the miner
names the per-hub pool that was bid on. PoolResolved carries finalize_by, the deadline of the
winner's unfilled reservation. A new ConfigChanged event fires from every admin setter, naming the
field, so Config changes are visible in the logs instead of only by polling.

All additions are appended last or are a new event, so decoders built against the previous shape
keep working. The Python decoder falls back to each event's previous shape, so events emitted
before the upgrade still decode. The packaged IDL is refreshed from the build.

Co-authored-by: anderdc <me@alexanderdc.com>

Bound event ingest per pass and cap its lookback at 6h (#792)

Ingest runs before the swap loop since #781, so a backlog it can't finish in one pass now blocks
every vote. A fresh database pages back to the program's first tx (~790k signatures) and a 5h+
outage decodes more than the watchdog allows; either restarts forever without voting.

Each pass now decodes at most 500 txs or 30s and stops the cursor there, so the backlog drains
across passes and a restart resumes. Paging never goes back further than 6h (the longest swap
life is ~5h); a cut is logged.

Co-authored-by: anderdc <me@alexanderdc.com>

fix(scripts): the curve-tail preview removes its ledger copies when it ends

The 9 Sep preview left one full ledger copy per tail in the executor's work
folder (6.1 GB), most of what filled the disk from 5 to 11 Oct. The copies are
now removed when the preview ends or fails, unless --keep is given.

fix(executor): unpacked images are removed even with read-only directories; stale ones are swept

rmtree(ignore_errors=True) gave up silently inside an image's read-only
directories, so parts of images could stay in the work folder after a run
(about 0.3 GB had collected by 17 Oct). Removal now makes such directories
writable and retries, and each daily run first sweeps sn21-img-* folders older
than six hours (never a running model or the forecast's warm image).

Bound validator reads of sandbox output files (#378)

* Bound validator reads of sandbox output files

Read sandbox output, inference stats and captured logs as plain regular
files with a size cap, shared with the local generated runner, so one
malformed or oversized file cannot stall or bloat the validator.

- Make evaluation directories sticky so the validator's own files stay
  in place, and start each run from an empty directory.
- Add a default validator memory limit (VALIDATOR_MEM_LIMIT, default 8g).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Keep partial output lines and stream inference stats

- OutputWatcher advances only through the last complete line, so an
  envelope still being written is read whole on the next poll.
- read_inference_stats iterates lines from the opened file instead of
  loading it whole; the size cap moves into open_regular_file.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Cap watcher reads and cover the preflight reader

- OutputWatcher reads at most up to the size cap rather than to a second
  unchecked size, still keeping a partly written last line for later.
- Log when inference stats are skipped for any reason but absence.
- Read preflight sandbox results through the same bounded reader.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Wrap long lines in touched code

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Create capture logs 0600 and size watcher reads to the file

- _open_capture passes an explicit 0o600 mode instead of os.open's 0o777
  default, so capture logs are never group/other writable.
- OutputWatcher reads up to the smaller of the file size and the cap,
  rather than requesting the whole cap on every poll.
- read_inference_stats skips a single invalid-UTF-8 line instead of
  abandoning the rest of the file.
- Preflight treats an unreadable sandbox output as no results, as before.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Close the descriptor when open_regular_file rejects a path

Check the raw descriptor before wrapping it and close it on any failure,
so a directory or other rejected path no longer leaks an fd per call.
Also set memswap_limit equal to mem_limit so the validator memory limit
is not extended by swap.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Apply the single-link check only to the local runner

The validator reads output.jsonl that the agent itself creates, so a
hard-link count check there let one extra link block every read. Make it
opt-in and keep it for the local generated runner, whose sandbox cannot
create links to the files it reads. Note VALIDATOR_MEM_LIMIT in the README.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Cap inference-stats reads while iterating

Count bytes as lines are read and drop the whole file if it passes the
cap, so a file that grows after the size check at open is still bounded.
Entries from a file are kept only once it has been read completely.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

---------

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

Bound per-evaluation sandbox disk use

* Bound per-evaluation sandbox disk use

A sandbox writes its output to a host-backed directory, so a single file
or a flood of files could otherwise consume host storage without limit.

- Give the sandbox a hard per-file write ceiling (--ulimit fsize), matching
  the 512 MiB output read cap.
- While the sandbox runs, the validator checks the bytes and file count the
  sandbox user has written to the evaluation directory, and kills the run
  and fails that evaluation if either passes its budget. Only the sandbox
  user's files count, and sparse files count only their allocated blocks.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Measure disk use by free space, not a name walk

A name-based walk of the evaluation directory misses disk a run consumes
through files it unlinks while still writing, directory floods, and
special files. Measure the filesystem's free space and free inodes
against a baseline instead (a single statvfs, cheap enough to poll every
loop), and check once more after the run. This catches those paths and
is simpler. Budget the bytes above the validator's own capped capture
logs written during the run.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Derive the per-file cap from the output read cap; tidy tests

Use MAX_SANDBOX_OUTPUT_BYTES for the fsize ulimit so the write ceiling
can't drift from the size the validator rejects on read, and drop an
unused variable in the budget test.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Keep the disk guard from raising inside the poll loop

A statvfs error must not propagate out of the guard: run_capped calls it
in the wait loop, where an exception would skip killing the child and
could wedge the reader-thread join. On a measurement error the guard now
returns no verdict instead.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Editor: make blur hide text, and move or resize a shape with any tool

Blur pixelated at half the picture's block whatever the size of the box,
so bold or large text stayed readable through it. It now pixelates at a
cell sized by the box (never finer than the picture's block, at most two
cells across the box's short side, capped at three blocks) and smooths
at the same radius, so no letter-scale contrast survives.

With a drawing tool active, pressing the handles or body of the shape
just drawn started a new shape. The selected shape's handles now resize
it and its body moves it whatever the tool, except crop and text; a

A row for an upload this device just made comes from the live sync
snapshot and carries neither the file's path on disk nor the server's
file id, so the viewer refused it ("This file can't be previewed"). Rows
like that also stayed pinned at the top of Recent Files after a batch
larger than the server's list, because they were only ever dropped once
the server listed them. Leaving the page rebuilt the feed, which is why
it worked after visiting Drive.

The viewer now asks Rust where such a row's file is on disk
(resolve_drive_file_source: only a drive synced here, and the path may
not leave the drive through .. or a symlink). A retained row is let go
once the snapshot no longer lists it and the server lists a newer upload
without it.

Edit image was offered only for a picture in an own drive synced on this
computer. capture_editor_open_file now takes the file's server id and,
when the file is not on disk, downloads it the way the viewer does and
edits that copy. Save goes back by upload into the file's own folder:
Replace uploads over it, Save a copy uploads an edited copy beside it.
Drives shared with the account are still refused.

The session's temp path is left empty so a save never writes the edited
picture into the preview cache, which is keyed by the original's
content and would otherwise show the old file's preview as the new one.

Drive's menu and the tray's Edit offer it for a row that carries its
server id, and pass the id and content hash through.

* Lay out Screenshots & Recording settings as tiles and cards

The tab was a stack of identical bordered rows. The two shortcuts now
lead it as side-by-side tiles with their keys drawn large, the capture
folder row can open the folder (Show in Finder, or Show in folder off
macOS) when the drive is synced here, the copy link, open link,
countdown and system audio choices are a grid of small cards, and each
setting's icon sits in a tinted chip. Columns follow the tab's width
through a container query. Every control, its words and what it calls
in Rust are unchanged.

* Split the remote editor wiring check into its own test

* Make dragging in the screenshot editor smooth

Each pointer move redrew the picture's shadow (a large blur), scaled the full screenshot down again, resized the canvas and re-rendered the editor. The shadow and picture are now drawn once per view into a backdrop that each frame copies, the canvas is only resized when its box changes, a drag updates at most once per screen frame, and hovering re-renders only when the cursor changes. Blur and pixelate are applied inside their own boxes instead of over the whole picture, with the same pixels as before.

* Offer Edit image in the file viewer

The viewer's top bar gets an Edit button beside Share, Download and Delete for the pictures the Drive row's Edit image covers (a PNG or JPEG in an own drive). It closes the viewer and opens the editor over the page.

* Capture card finishes on its own upload, not the whole sync (#549)

* Let a capture card finish on its own link, not the whole sync

A synced capture's card waited for the sync engine to reach its file, even when its share link (its own encrypted copy) was already on the server. It now finishes as soon as the link is public and the engine has not started on the file; a file the engine is uploading still shows its progress.

* Retry a capture's link, and keep the card up when it fails

Making a capture's share link failed once on a dropped connection (the server answered a second later), so nothing was copied or opened, and the card treated the failed link as finished and slid away. The link is now tried three times in all (1 s, then 3 s) unless the drive is full, and a card whose link failed stays up with Create link.

* Write Mac recordings with their index first (#551)

The finished MP4 had its index after the video, so a browser asked for the end of the file first and a share link (readable only from the start) downloaded the whole recording before the first frame. The recorder now sets shouldOptimizeForNetworkUse, so the file is ftyp, moov, mdat and plays from the first bytes. Windows and Linux already write fragmented files with the index first; a test pins all three.

* Keep the recording bar still when a menu opens; add controls on the camera bubble (#552)

The recording bar jumped up when its microphone or camera menu opened.
The pill's window grows upward to hold the menu, but the page was laid out
for the old size and anchored to the top until Rust's answer came back, so
the pill was drawn at the top of the grown window, a menu's height above
where it was, until the menu arrived. A webview also keeps its old picture
at the top of a grown window until it draws again.

On macOS the pill's page is now laid out once with room for a menu above
and below the pill, and the window only shows the slice it needs.
set_pill_frame places the page inside the window in the same main-thread
turn as the window, with screen updates held, so opening a menu moves the
window's edge over a page that never changes size. Elsewhere the page asks
which side the menu will open on (capture_controls_menu_side), anchors the
pill to the edge that stays put, and only then asks for the room.

The camera bubble now has its own controls while recording: the bubble's
sizes and pause / resume, shown on hover. The bubble's window is filmed, so
the controls are a window of their own over it, which every recorder leaves
out (the macOS helper films only the main window and the bubble of
Hippius's windows; Windows protects the window; Linux has none). They are
shown from Rust's pointer watch and call the same commands as the pill.

* Fix two flaky capture checks: Xvfb resets and recorder start time (#553)

Linux: Xvfb resets itself whenever its last client disconnects, so the
X11 capture test, which opens one connection after another, could
connect mid-reset and get "Connection reset by peer" or no pointer.
with-xvfb.sh now starts Xvfb with -noreset.

Windows: the file's time zero was the first picture, but the H.264
encoder is made from that picture and `started` is only sent after it,
which takes 1.5 to 2.2 s on a hosted runner. That wait was recorded at
the start of every file, as a frozen opening picture. Time zero is now
when the encoder is ready and Start is answered; pictures from the wait
become the opening picture. The file also ends when Stop was asked,
not after the sources finished shutting down. Linux shares the writer
loop and gets the same fix.

The runtime test now compares the file with the time it measured as
recording, so a slow sleep on a busy runner cannot fail it, while a
kept pause or a recorded warm-up still does.

* Measure the recorded time in the pause test instead of assuming it

start_pause_resume_stop_leaves_a_file_with_the_pause_cut_out slept
0.3 s, paused 0.4 s, slept 0.3 s and required the file to end between
0.45 and 0.90 s. On a busy macOS runner the sleeps ran long and the file
ended at 0.94 s, failing the staging run.

The test now reads the clock just before and just after start, pause,
resume and stop. The child stamps each one when it reads the command, so
those readings bracket every stamp however slow the machine is. The file
must sit between the time certainly recorded and the time that could
have been, a frame either way; neither includes the pause, so a pause
left in the file still fails. Passed 30 of 30 runs with every core busy.

* Open Settings with Cmd+comma from the main window

The shortcut only worked while the menu bar window had the keyboard. The
main window now answers it too, with the same key rule and route as the
menu bar window's menu, so the two cannot drift.

* Show the recording controls again on macOS

Since the pill's page was made taller than its window, so a menu could
open without moving the pill, the page sticks out above the window while
no menu is open. WebKit took that part for a title bar and cut it off the
page's viewport with its automatic content insets, so the page was laid
out 300 points lower and the pill sat below its window: a recording
showed only the camera bubble. set_pill_frame now turns the insets off
before it places the page, so the viewport is the page's whole frame.

* Make screen recordings smaller on every platform

A lower average bit rate (5 Mbps at 1080p, 1 to 10 Mbps by pixel count)
and a keyframe every 4 s instead of 2 s, shared by the Mac helper and the
Windows and Linux recorders through sizing::RateControl. Windows asks the
encoder for peak-constrained VBR; Linux puts each GStreamer encoder in a
mode that spends less on a still screen, capped at twice the average.
Text stays as sharp; files are about half the size.

* Keep the recording controls and camera bubble on top on GNOME Wayland

* Fit the Wayland record panel to its bar, and let the dock bring Hippius back on Linux

The Wayland panel was a fixed 520 x 600 window drawn as a dark framed box
around a small bar. It is now transparent, opens small, and is sized to the
bar and any open menu (capture_panel_fit, only while choosing on Wayland,
clamped by panel_window_size); menus open downward.

During a recording a dock click did nothing. GNOME's dock raises the app's
first visible window: on Wayland that was the controls bar (GTK 3 cannot keep
it off the dock), and on X11 the hidden main window left nothing to raise.
X11 now minimizes the main window instead of hiding it, so the dock restores
it. Wayland keeps it hidden (a minimized window needs an activation token
GNOME refuses) and focus_watch_gtk brings it forward when a capture window
takes the keyboard while the pointer is elsewhere, past a grace period after
the window was shown. A second launch now does what the tray's Open Hippius
does, and a main window minimized before a capture stays minimized.

* Use Hippius's own capture bar for screenshots on Linux Wayland

A Wayland screenshot no longer opens the desktop's screenshot tool. Hippius
takes one non-interactive still of the whole desktop through the Screenshot
portal, cuts it into one slice per GDK monitor, and shows the usual overlay
full screen on each monitor over its slice, with the same bar, keys, timer
and instant shortcut as other platforms. Area and entire screen only, since
Wayland lists no windows. The chosen area is cut out of the still in the
overlay's CSS pixels times the slice's pixels per logical pixel, so HiDPI
and fractional scaling map without extra cases.

With the timer the overlay hides the still and counts over the live screen,
and a fresh still is taken once the overlays are gone. When the portal
refuses the still or it does not fit the monitor layout, the desktop's own
interactive tool takes over as before. Switching the bar to Record swaps the
overlays for the recording panel, and back.

Surfaces now says how a screenshot is chosen (selection) apart from how a
recording is (record_selection), and each overlay is told whether it is the
panel or frozen, so the frontend never checks the platform.

* Get the camera working on Ubuntu 22.04, and log every camera step

On PipeWire older than 0.3.64 (Ubuntu 22.04 ships 0.3.48), the PipeWire
device provider hides the V4L2 one when gstreamer1.0-pipewire is
installed, so WebKitGTK opened every camera through pipewiresrc, which
often never delivers a picture there. A browser on the same machine opens
/dev/video* directly and works. At startup Hippius reads the PipeWire
version and, below 0.3.64, sets
GST_PLUGIN_FEATURE_RANK=pipewiredeviceprovider:NONE for its web processes
and the recorder child, so cameras open through v4l2src. Screen recording
asks for pipewiresrc by name and is unaffected. A rank the user set is
left alone.

A capture page that finished loading before its media stream was turned
on is loaded again. The camera page reports each step to the app log as
`camera:` lines (throttled), retries once when no frame arrives within
8 s, and then says the camera is unavailable instead of pulsing on its
placeholder for ever.

* Pass the encoder setting's key as a raw pointer (clippy::borrow_as_ptr on Windows)

* Pin that only the panel is fitted, and never during a frozen screenshot

* Allow the Windows runtime pause test three quarters of the pause as slack

A hosted Windows runner read a 3.00 s recording as 3.54 s, 0.04 s over
the half-pause margin, and failed PRs that changed only Linux code. The
margin is now 0.75 s: still under the 1 s pause, so a pause kept in the
file fails, and far under the encoder's 1.5 to 2.2 s warm-up.

* Ride out stalled package mirrors in CI

Two outside outages failed CI today. GitHub's Ubuntu mirror stopped
answering and apt hung until release-deps-linux's 15-minute timeout
cancelled it, and the Chocolatey feed answered 504, so the Windows
runtime job had no ffprobe. apt now gives each request a 30 s timeout and
retries it five times (an apt.conf.d entry written by the shared install
script), and the ffprobe step retries Chocolatey three times.

* Play videos in the Linux file viewer from a loopback stream

WebKitGTK plays media through GStreamer, whose WebKit source element
(webkitwebsrc) claims only http, https and blob. A video on Tauri's
asset:// scheme never reaches wry's handler, so the player sat on a black
frame (WebKit bug 146351 and tauri#3725, both open). The viewer therefore
offered only the system player on Linux.

Linux now plays from http://127.0.0.1:<random port>/v/<token>, served by
hyper (already built for reqwest; only its server features are added):

- one random 256-bit token per opened file, minted only for the main
  window and only after the viewer's preview gate; it expires when idle
  or after its lifetime, is refused for any other signed-in account, is
  released when the viewer closes, and logout stops the server
- the path is re-canonicalised on every request, Host is checked, GET and
  HEAD only, byte ranges with 206/416, Accept-Ranges, Content-Range and a
  content type from the extension, streamed in chunks, no CORS headers
- CSP allows http://127.0.0.1:* in media-src only

The recorder child's probe also reports the H.264 and AAC decoders
GStreamer would pick. Without an H.264 decoder the viewer names the
package to install (gstreamer1.0-libav, or the Fedora equivalent) and
offers the system player and Download. A stream that errors or shows no
frame within a few seconds falls back the same way instead of spinning.
macOS and Windows keep the asset URL.

input so x264 can never pick High 4:4:4 Predictive.

in autoHide.ts, pure and unit tested.

Keyboard focus in the card holds it the way the pointer does, as the
recording pill opens on pointing or on focus. Only focus that draws the
ring counts: a button's focus after a click does not, and neither does a
window that has lost focus. A focused menu item that closes its menu
takes the focus with it, so the hold is read again after every render.

* Say where the keyboard holds the capture card in the changelog

The card is never the key window on macOS, so its buttons are reached
from the keyboard on Windows and Linux only.

* Pin that a card pointed at as it settles starts its countdown held

The pointer can be on the card while it uploads; once the link settles,
the countdown starts paused and the whole time is there on leaving.

* chore(release): 0.6.12-beta.1

* Show the Hippius name next to the logo in the tray popover

The popover's header showed only the logo, so it did not say which app
it belongs to. It now uses the main window's own lockup
(HippiusBrandMark): the logo and the name on one line before the
balance, at the popover's larger logo size. In dark mode the name takes
the popover's dark brand tone, like the Balance label. Windows shows the
same popover; Linux has none, its tray opens a menu.

Only the name may give way: it truncates while the balance pill never
shrinks, so a long balance with the chat and bell badges keeps the
balance and the menu in view in the 460px window.

* Put Record before Screenshot wherever the two sit together

Most captures are recordings, so Record now leads every place the two
are offered side by side:

- the tray popover's tiles: Record, Screenshot, Upload
- the capture bar's mode groups: Record's three modes, then Screenshot's
- the Record and Screenshot buttons (Captures page and its empty state,
  the folder list's header, the in-drive toolbar, Overview's Recent
  Files)
- the empty states' wording: "Record your screen or take a screenshot"

A Record that this computer cannot use keeps its first place, dimmed
with the reason, so the layout never rearranges between machines. The
keyboard shortcuts and the keys each control shows are unchanged.

* Keep the live folder-delete test off the empty-drive hold

locally_deleted_empty_folder_not_resurrected deletes the only folder of
an otherwise empty drive. Since #531, guard_empty_walk holds folder
changes for exactly that shape (no directory walked, folders cached,
drive folder visibly empty), because an unmounted disk or an evicted
cloud folder looks the same. The test therefore failed against a live
server: Doomed stayed registered.

The hold is the intended behaviour, so fix the test: put a user file in
the drive root so the delete is not the empty-drive shape.

Add deleting_last_folder_of_empty_drive_is_held to pin the hold end to
end: over two combined cycles the folder stays registered on the
server, is not recreated on disk, and keeps its cache row so the delete
applies once the hold lifts.

* Prove the empty-drive hold lifts in the live hold test

Review of #611: a closed gate from an unreadable mass-delete record or an
unresolvable config dir would also pass the two held cycles, so the test
could not tell the #531 empty-walk guard from those. After the held
cycles, write a user file and assert the next cycle applies the delete
(unregistered on the server, cache row dropped). That rules out the other
closed gates and checks the "applies once the hold lifts" claim.

Also update the module doc to name the hold test.

RUSTSEC-2026-0346 to 0349 were published against rustls 0.23.45, and
cargo deny fails on them. Only rustls moves (cargo update -p rustls).
No changelog entry: nothing a user sees changes.

* Put the recording shortcut before the screenshot one in Settings

Record leads wherever the two sit together, and the Screenshots &
Recording tab still showed the screenshot shortcut's tile first. Only the
order changes: the keys, the commands and the tile hidden where this
computer cannot record stay as they were.

* Bump rustls to 0.23.46 for four new advisories

cargo-deny's supply-chain gate fails on advisories published 2026-10-14
against rustls 0.23.45, all patched in 0.23.46:

- RUSTSEC-2026-0346: Debug impls for client session values expose TLS
  secrets
- RUSTSEC-2026-0347: buffered application data sent to the outer server
  after ECH rejection
- RUSTSEC-2026-0348: Brotli certificate decompression can allocate up to
  1 GiB before authentication
- RUSTSEC-2026-0349: an unauthenticated ServerHello can downgrade later
  connections to classical key exchange

The tree has a single rustls (0.23.x), so this is a lockfile-only patch
bump with no other crate changes.

hcfs #683 (thenervelab/hcfs#665): once the server advertises
folder_share_link_envelopes, a folder link carries a per-link secret and
the server keeps the drive key sealed under it. Pin hcfs at main 3854bb9e
merged with #667's head (still open, and this pin already depends on it).

The member mint sends the envelope too and revokes a mint whose envelope
the server did not keep. The keystore stores link secrets under their own
kinds (rebuilding an older CHECK), and the owner wrap sets flag 0x04 so an
older device cannot rebuild a link secret as a #k= link.

The listing reports each link's format, and Reshare replaces a legacy
link minted here with a link-secret one for the same folder, then revokes
the old link.

A folder link minted before link secrets carries the key to the whole
drive. Where Rust offers it, the row is marked Old link, the menu offers

note when the old link could not be turned off.
